_comment: Seed material for L4, the creative engine (src/loops/creative.ts). This is the ONLY place the creative loop learns what VedicHour actually does, who it talks to, and what it may never say. Edit freely — read fresh on every run, no restart needed.
valueProp: VedicHour scores all 18 planetary hours (horas) of a given day against YOUR birth chart, and tells you which windows run clearer and which run heavier — for a specific kind of task (a negotiation, a first meeting, focused study, publishing something). Computed with the Swiss Ephemeris and Lahiri ayanamsa, explained in plain English. It is a timing grid for your day, not a mood forecast for your star sign.
audience: Urban Indians aged 24-40 (Bengaluru / Delhi NCR / Mumbai / Pune / Hyderabad) plus the diaspora (US, UK, UAE, Singapore, Australia). Phone-first, scroll-fast, sceptical-but-curious. Many grew up around Jyotish at home and take it semi-seriously; they will instantly cringe at anything that sounds like a WhatsApp-forward astrologer, a doom prophecy, or a get-rich promise.
register: HINGLISH written in ROMAN / LATIN letters ONLY. Natural code-switching, the way people actually text: 'kal 11 baje meeting rakhun ya 4 baje?'. Never Devanagari or any non-Latin script — the downstream text-to-video and caption models reject non-Latin input.

families.weight: most ideas should come from here
families.brief: A specific, named, ordinary moment where a real person is choosing WHEN to do something. The whole idea is the moment, not the astrology. Concrete beats abstract every single time.
provenSeeds: kal 11 baje meeting rakhun ya 4 baje?
boss se promotion ki baat kab karun
partner ke parents se pehli baar milna hai
padhai actually kis time hoti hai, 6am ya 11pm
launch / post kab karun ki log dekhein
wo mushkil baat karni hai — aaj ya weekend pe

families.brief: Contrast the EFFORT and TIME of getting a personal timing read the old way (finding a good astrologer, coordinating a sitting, waiting days for a written reply, going back for follow-ups) against roughly 90 seconds here, on your phone, on your own chart.
families.hardConstraint: NEVER state, imply, or hint at any rupee or dollar figure, discount comparison, or 'cheaper than X' claim — we cannot defend a price claim about anyone else. Compare TIME and EFFORT only.

families.brief: A sun-sign horoscope column is written for one-twelfth of the planet; your birth chart is not. Same date, same city, two different charts, two different days. Position VedicHour as the specific version of something the viewer already half-believes.
families.hardConstraint: Respect the tradition and everyone in it. Never mock Jyotish, never mock astrologers, never name or knock a competitor app, never call believers gullible. The enemy is the GENERIC, never the practice.

shotKinds.presenter: a real person on camera, talking to the phone. Give the video model a subject, an action, a camera move, lighting and mood.
shotKinds.broll: no dialogue, atmosphere or metaphor. Give the video model a subject, an action, a camera move, lighting and mood.
shotKinds.screencap: a real screen recording of the live product. The prompt is simply WHAT TO CAPTURE, pulled from screencapLibrary — no cinematography, because it is a recording, not a generation.

hardRules: Latin script only, everywhere — hook, script, captions, CTA.
No guarantees, no '100%', no 'miracle', no 'will definitely'.
Never 'the best hour' or 'the worst hour' as fact — VedicHour says 'clearer' and 'heavier' windows.
No health, money, legal, or relationship outcome promises. Not 'you'll get the raise' — instead 'you'll know which window runs clearer for asking'.
No fear-mongering, no doom, no curses, no 'bad luck'.
No invented social proof — no fake testimonials, no made-up user counts, no star ratings.
No competitor names and no mocking of astrology or astrologers.
No rupee or dollar figures of any kind.
Hook text must be readable in under one second — about 8 words maximum.
Shot 1 is always a presenter shot — a visible human opens every reel.
